item.title: Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro Puts ‘Guardrails’ on Data Centers
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro ordered strict new guardrails on data centers in the state as local opposition grows against developers.

item.title: Ex-Tricolor Executives Face SEC Lawsuit After Firm Collapse
item.description: Tricolor Holdings founder Daniel Chu, who already faces federal charges, and two other former executives were sued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission for allegedly defrauding investors before the used car seller and subprime lender imploded.

item.title: Trump Overhaul Prompts Dulles Board to Seek $14 Billion in Bonds
item.description: The governing board that oversees Washington Dulles International Airport will vote Wednesday on whether to add $15.5 billion to its capital budget to finance the airport’s multi-year overhaul backed by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Boeing-Lockheed Space Venture Inks $1.5 Billion Private Bonds
item.description: Boeing Co. and Lockheed Martin Corp.’s rocket joint venture is wrapping up a $1.5 billion private-bond deal that’s been tripled in size.

item.title: TikTok Is Exploring Feature to Send Money Over Direct Messages
item.description: TikTok is exploring a feature that would allow users to send money to each other in direct messages, in a move that would extend the social media app’s push into financial services.

item.title: Five Grain Ships Struck Near Russian Black Sea Ports
item.description: At least five grain ships have been attacked near the Russian Black Sea ports of Novorossiysk and Tuapse as Moscow struggles to continue exporting grain amid heightened Ukrainian strikes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: OpenAI Makes AI Safety Changes in Wake of Hugging Face Breach
item.description: OpenAI said it’s implementing more aggressive systems to monitor and safeguard artificial intelligence models under development after recent cybersecurity incidents ignited concerns about AI tools running amok.

item.title: Walter Probe Weighs on Carvana as Investors Suspect Share Sale
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. are extending losses Tuesday, hurt by concerns that one of the company’s largest investors — billionaire Mark Walter — may sell down his stake as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.

item.title: University of California System Offloads $1 Billion of Private Equity Stakes
item.description: The University of California system sold $1 billion of private equity stakes to HarbourVest Partners, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Meta Exploits Youths on Social Media, States Allege at Trial
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. has deceived the public for years by targeting children on Facebook and Instagram with technology designed to turn them into compulsive users and drive up advertising revenue, a lawyer at the California attorney general’s office told a jury.

item.title: French Tax Office to Use AI to Probe Vulnerabilities After Hack
item.description: The French tax office is planning to use artificial intelligence tools to probe for weaknesses after it was targeted by a cyberattack that exposed personal details of hundreds of thousands of taxpayers.

item.title: Israel’s Central Bank Chief Says Next Rate Decision Is ‘Live’
item.description: Israel’s central bank governor kept options open for an upcoming interest-rate decision, saying policymakers are dealing with high levels of uncertainty.

item.title: Port of LA Has Near-Record July as Importers Navigate Trade War
item.description: The Port of Los Angeles had its second-busiest July on record, as importers navigated global supply chain disruptions and volatile tariff policy.

item.title: Anthropic Pre-IPO Credit Facility Set to Climb Past $10 Billion
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s revolving credit facility is set to rise above its roughly $10 billion target, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence firm prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering.

item.title: Thoma Bravo Weighs Concessions in $2 Billion Sophos Refinancing
item.description: Thoma Bravo-backed software firm Sophos is focusing on existing lenders to refinance or extend more than $2 billion of loans as soon as next month, after efforts to secure private credit backing faltered, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: BP Joins Venezuelan Oil Trade to Challenge Trafigura and Vitol
item.description: BP Plc has become the latest foreign company to begin trading Venezuelan oil since the US removed former President Nicolás Maduro, following in the footsteps of Trafigura Group and Vitol Group.

item.title: JPMorgan’s Santos Says ‘AI Tentacle’ Risk Spans Bonds and Stocks
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management’s Gabriela Santos warned that “AI-factor” concentration risk has spread beyond equities into fixed income, ratcheting up the need for investor caution even as the super-cycle thesis remains intact.

item.title: Starwood Team Lends $672 Million for US Outdoor Storage Lots
item.description: Starwood Property Trust Inc. and Realterm, a global investment manager focused on transportation, provided a $672 million loan for a group of US industrial outdoor storage lots.

item.title: Apple Lowers App Store Fees in Europe to Settle Dispute With EU
item.description: Apple Inc. has agreed to a set of sweeping changes for its App Store in Europe, including dropping per-install fees for developers who don’t use the iPhone marketplace, to resolve a dispute with the European Union over competition concerns.

item.title: Bitcoin Whales End Selling Spree, Adding $2.9 Billion in 60 Days
item.description: Bitcoin has spent months mired in a slump that has driven out retail traders, drained billions from crypto funds and turned one of its biggest buyers into a seller. Now, investors searching for signs of a bottom are getting a modicum of relief from an old source: Bitcoin whales are buying again.

item.title: Raw Sugar Advances to 14-Month High on Global Supply Concerns
item.description: Raw sugar futures rose to the highest in more than a year as India, the world’s second-largest producer, is considering cutting import duties on the commodity in the latest sign of global supply constraint.

item.title: Colombian GDP Growth Jumped to 3.5% in Boost for New Government
item.description: Colombian growth beat expectations in the second quarter, handing President Abelardo de la Espriella a buoyant economy as he starts his four-year term.

item.title: BofA Sees Nvidia Trading at Up to 50% Discount on AI Risks
item.description: Nvidia Corp. shares could be trading at a discount of as much as 50%, as investors overstate risks related to the leader in artificial intelligence chips, according to Bank of America.

item.title: What Are Flock Cameras? Why Are They So Controversial?
item.description: Thousands of US cities and towns have installed surveillance tools made by Flock Safety, a fast-growing Atlanta startup. The connected devices, such as sensors and automated license plate readers, have allowed law-enforcement agencies to map vehicles’ travel over long distances, which, they say, bolsters their ability to fight crime. But critics contend the network of cameras amounts to mass surveillance.

item.title: Blackstone-Backed QTS Kicks Off Data-Center Bond at Hefty Cost
item.description: Blackstone-backed QTS Realty Trust Inc. units kicked off a high-grade bond sale to help fund construction of a data center tied to Microsoft Corp., offering a hefty yield to drum up demand from investors who’ve become more selective about what they’re willing to buy.

item.title: Russia’s Oil Exports Extend Their Slump Amid Ukrainian Drone Strikes
item.description: Shipments fell for a fifth week with no crude loading from the key Novorossiysk oil terminal in the seven days to Aug. 16

item.title: Real Estate Firm Avison Young Plans Deals After Recapitalization
item.description: Avison Young (Canada) Inc. is plotting growth and acquisitions after creditors swapped debt for equity in the Toronto-based real estate advisory group.

item.title: Energy Stocks Soar to Record as Oil Rises on Trump’s Hard Line
item.description: Energy stocks are closing in on record levels reached earlier this year amid the Middle East war as investors see diminishing prospects for a near-term ceasefire that could ease the standoff in the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: ByteDance Draws Over $30 Billion in Orders for Jumbo Bank Loan
item.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has attracted more than $30 billion of orders for its jumbo syndicated loan, people familiar with the matter said, indicating strong interest from lenders as the Chinese technology giant ramps up investments in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Chile’s Economy Unexpectedly Stalls in Fresh Setback for Kast
item.description: Chile’s economy unexpectedly stalled in the second quarter, representing a blow for President José Antonio Kast as his administration works to revive investment and employment.
